Header: Phytophthora spp., Pythium spp., Rhizoctonia spp., Fusarium spp. Tanay ki Saran

Prevention: Maintain proper spacing, 12 to 18-inches plant to plant and 24 to 30-inches row to row.
Supply adequate moisture but do not over water and avoid working with plants when the soil is wet.
Disinfect tools and containers with one part bleach in four parts water or with 70% rubbing alcohol (isopropyl).
Solarize the soil for 21 days prior to transplantation with plastic sheet.
Then, remove the plastic and leave the bed for up to 3 days.
Keep good air circulation around plant seedlings, and don’t plant seeds too deep.
Plant only high-quality seed or vigorous transplants and avoid soil that is poorly drained.
Monitoring: In a nursery, the disease may appear in patches in 2-4 days, the entire lot of seedling may be destroyed.
Disease incidence and severity is increased by cold temperatures, over watering, high humidity and overcrowding.
This disease is more prevalent in nurseries.
Seeds may decay, fail to emerge or once emerged develop water soaked discoloured areas on the stems which withers and causes the plant to fall over.
Direct Control: Sulphur powder, or a tea of seaweed, garlic or chamomile as a botanical control to treat small areas of infection.
Pseudomonas fluorescens 10 g/ kg of seed 24 hours before sowing as biological control of damping off.
Restrictions: Keep pesticides out of reach of children
Always wear protective clothing, such as mask, rubber boots, gloves
Dispose of containers responsibly (Do not clean containers in canals)
Drench immediately after planting with copper based fungicide.
If damping-off occurs continue to apply fungicides at weekly intervals.
Damping off may be suppressed with
U (Unlikely to present acute hazard for all chemicals)
